thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: `hosted-inference-5xx-surge` fired for service `hosted-inference` 
Trigger: 5xx > 20% over 3m. Primary on-call (sam) paged.

monitoring-bot: anomaly detected: spike in 5xx originating from node-pool `gpux-3-us-east`. Error class: downstream datastore timeouts + transient KV evictions.

sam (on-call): ack? trying mobile. on call laptop but getting a weird error on slack notifications. looking now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: primary did not acknowledge within 90s. Escalating to secondary (ida).

ida (secondary): picking up. joining bridge: https://g.stack.redwood.com/bridges/inc-2198800000. @sam if you can still join please do. I'll take lead if you need rest.

sam (on-call): joined. my phone was on Do Not Disturb (family emergency). I can stay on for handoff. tl;dr: large spike, customers seeing timeouts. thanks for taking lead ida.

sue (support): CS: multiple customers reporting generation failures and timeouts across EU/US. Top-5 affected apps listed in ticket INC-9876. Customers asking for ETA.

ida (secondary): first actions: 1) temporarily silence noisy alerts to avoid paging churn, 2) reduce concurrency for high-risk routes, 3) isolate bad hosts. Doing (1) now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: manager escalation timer hit — paging manager (harper) per policy due to missed primary ack window.

harper (manager): called. hopping on bridge. need a concise incident state and customer impact. assign me owner if escalation continues.

devin (infra): running `kubectl get pods -n hosted | grep gpux-3-us-east` shows 6 pods with repeated `KVEvictError` and `DatastoreTimeout`. I'll cordon node `ip-10-3-45-7` and drain pods from that host.

ida (secondary): please don't drain everything at once — do rolling drain with maxUnavailable=1. I'll shift 20% of traffic to dedicated fallback fleet: `hosted-dedicated-small`.

sam (on-call): performing route-split: `POST /admin/route-split` {"route":"/v1/generate","fallback":"hosted-dedicated-small","percentage":20}. Applied — monitoring.

matt: telemetry: after split, 5xx dropped from 22% -> 14% in 2m. Latency slightly increased for fallback but within SLO for lower-priority customers.

sue (support): sending customer update: "We are actively mitigating an error spike affecting a subset of generation requests. We have a temporary fallback in place; some customers may notice higher latency. Engineers are working on fix. ETA ~15-30m." Will update top customers.

devin (infra): cordon/drain started for ip-10-3-45-7. Restarted kube-proxy and restarted kubelet on that host. Observability: pod memory pressure was high — logs show repeated cache eviction loops.

ida (secondary): good. also increasing KV cache size on the pool config to reduce eviction pressure: `kubectl apply -f kvcache-bump.yaml -n hosted` — applying as a rolling config update.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: primary now acknowledged. (sam) is back in channel.

sam (on-call): back and standing down from lead, handing to ida. I'll support verification.

harper (manager): thanks. what are current customer-impact metrics?

matt: pre-mitigation: timeouts near 3% of requests overall, post-mitigation (split + cordon + cache bump): 0.9%. Still above baseline but within short-term acceptable threshold.

ida (secondary): can we confirm the root cause? it looks like a memory leak or config regression on `runtime-allocator` released yesterday 02:30 UTC. Any rollout IDs?

devin (infra): rollout `runtime-allocator@2026-02-18-0230` is correlated. I'll roll that change back on a single canary. If errors drop, we'll do full rollback.

matt: canary rollback started. 1 pod reverted, errors on canary pod fell to baseline. Good signal. Rolling remainder with maxSurge=0 to avoid capacity dip.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: manager (harper) acknowledged.

harper (manager): great. please ensure CS banner includes the rollback note and an ETA. Keep me posted on any escalations.

sue (support): banner updated. customers notified of the rollback and fallback routing. No critical escalations so far.

ida (secondary): rollback completed cluster-wide. Observability: 5xx now 0.7% and falling. Rolling restarts finished with no further regressions.

sam (on-call): verifying, running smoke tests against critical routes. All green.

harper (manager): marking incident as mitigated when verified by infra and SRE. Requesting short postmortem w/ timeline, who paged, why primary didn't ack (DND), and steps to prevent future silent-ack scenarios.

ida (secondary): assigning postmortem owners: devin for RCA (allocator regression), sam for alerting/ack flow, sue for customer comms. Will draft mitigation plan: add canary gate for allocator changes and PD escalation phone fallback.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: MITIGATED. PagerDuty incident closed.

sue (support): will consolidate tickets and attach banner + customer responses.

devin (infra): opening PR to require KV-metrics stability for allocator deploys and add a quick rollback job. Target: PR by EOD.

matt: adding monitoring alert to detect sudden KV eviction rate deltas (>=3x baseline in 2m).

harper (manager): nice work team. bridge closing in 15m. Postmortem due tomorrow EOW. :thumbsup:
